To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-2/ IFN therapy was superior to IL-2 alone, IFN alone, LAK alone, or LAK/IFN therapy for treatment of pulmonary metastases.
the combination of IFN-alpha and IL-2 is more effective than either alone in treating pulmonary metastases.
IFN-alpha augmented therapy of metastases with interleukin 2 (IL- 2) is more effective than IL-2 therapy alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel immunotherapeutic strategies to improve the efficacy of current treatment modalities for the treatment of cancer.
the development of new and effective immunotherapy for cancer.
developing new approaches in the immunotherapy of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-2 and IFN-alpha A/D are synergistic in vivo in the treatment of metastases.
IL-2/ IFN therapy was superior in the therapy of both early and late metastases, with no added benefit to the addition of LAK.
IFN-alpha A/D (50,000 u) plus IL-2 (25,000 u) is superior to either alone in treatment of early and late metastases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of IL-2 with IFN is more effective in treating metastases than IL-2 or LAK alone, and is more effective in prolonging survival than LAK or IL-2 plus LAK.
the combination of IL-2 and IFN-alpha is a simple, safe, and effective therapy of metastatic disease.
the IL-2/ IFN combination therapy is superior to IL-2, IL-2/Lak, IFN, IFN/Lak and IFN alone in the treatment of both early Day-3 and advanced Day-10 pulmonary metastases in the C57BL/10 mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFN can be combined with IL-2 to enhance the antitumor activity of IL-2 and that this combination can be used to enhance the antipulmonary metastasis activity of IL-1.

the combination of interferon-alpha with interleukin 2 is more effective than either of these agents alone, and is more effective than the combination of interferons with lymphokine activated killers.
